title: Noor and the Veil
premise: Ada Delacroix has spent her life keeping the smuggler's guild of Thornfell invisible, but when prayers to the old gods start being answered with fire and omens, she learns her guild was founded as the last wardens of a broken covenant between the mortal realm and the divine. The covenant's keystone—a living memory held in Ada's bloodline—must be carried to the Veilstone before the moon completes its thirteenth turn, or both realms will starve each other into silence. Hunted by a zealot order that wants the gods dead and tempted by Kaelen, an exiled god's mortal son who offers her escape instead of duty, Ada must choose between survival and sacrifice. In the end she reforges the covenant by surrendering her own memories of everyone she loves, sealing the Veilstone at the cost of forgetting why it mattered—until Kaelen, now mortal, spends his final years helping her remember.
about_author: Ansel Voss is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping remote mountain passes before turning to fiction. Their work blends folklore, geography, and quiet heartbreak into fantasy that asks what we owe the places that raised us.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon Rises
chapters.summary: Ada Delacroix guides a smuggling run through the Thornfell passes, establishing her mastery of hidden roads and her guild's precarious decline. When a prayer whispered in a ruined shrine is answered by a burning sigil in the sky, her carefully invisible world cracks. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: unease beneath competence—the first sign that hiding can no longer protect her.

chapters.title: What the Guild Buried
chapters.summary: Ada confronts Guildmaster Sorrel about the omen; he reveals fragments of the truth: the guild were once wardens of a covenant between realms, broken three generations ago. He refuses to say what role her family played. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: betrayal and disorientation as the foundation of her identity proves a lie.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Villages near the Veil report answered prayers turning destructive—wishes granted with cruel literalism. Ada witnesses a farmer's plea for rain become a flood. She realizes the gods are returning blind and starving for worship. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: dawning horror and compassion for powers gone feral.

chapters.title: The Zealot Order
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Maren Voss arrives in Thornfell hunting 'god-touched' heresy, burning shrines and interrogating smugglers. Ada narrowly evades capture using her secret roads. POV: Ada, with a brief interlude from Maren's perspective revealing her genuine conviction. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Kaelen at the Crossroads
chapters.summary: Ada catches a stranger poaching her routes: Kaelen, charming and secretive, who knows things about the old gods no mortal should. He claims to seek the Veilstone too—and offers her a way out of Thornfell entirely. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: wary attraction tangled with suspicion.

chapters.title: Blood Remembers
chapters.summary: Sorrel, dying from wounds taken protecting guild records, confesses: Ada's bloodline carries the covenant's keystone memory. Only a Delacroix can reforge it. He gives her a fractured map and dies asking forgiveness. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: grief fused with terrible inheritance.

chapters.title: Roads That No Longer Exist
chapters.summary: Ada and Kaelen travel toward the first waypoint, but the mountains themselves are shifting as the veil thins—old paths lead to places erased decades ago. They survive an ambush by Maren's soldiers. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: trust slowly built through shared danger.

chapters.title: The God Who Chose Mortality
chapters.summary: Kaelen reveals he is the mortal son of Veyra, goddess of thresholds, who abandoned divinity to break the covenant's cruelty. His father's return threatens everything Veyra sacrificed. POV: Kaelen. Emotional beat: vulnerability—he has been using Ada as much as helping her, and hates himself for it.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn, First Shadow
chapters.summary: The moon begins its thirteenth turn; time distorts in Thornfell. A village Ada loves is trapped in a loop of its own happiest day, worshippers unwilling to leave. She must shatter their paradise to free them. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: the first true taste of the price the covenant demands.

chapters.title: Maren's Sermon
chapters.summary: Captured by Maren's order, Ada debates theology with her captor over days of imprisonment. Maren believes the gods' return is humanity's punishment for dependence; only total severance will save mortals. POV: alternating Ada and Maren. Emotional beat: grudging mutual respect between enemies.

chapters.title: Escape Through the Hollow Road
chapters.summary: Kaelen trades a fragment of his fading divinity to buy Ada's freedom, revealing his power—and his dwindling mortality—to Maren's order. They flee into the Hollow Road, a passage through the underworld's edge. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: love confessed in extremis, shadowed by what it may cost.

chapters.title: The Underworld's Toll
chapters.summary: In the Hollow Road, travelers pay tolls in memory. Ada pays small recollections to pass; Kaelen secretly pays larger ones to shield her. She notices him forgetting pieces of himself. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: tenderness and dread—she sees her own future reflected in him.

chapters.title: Veyra's Threshold
chapters.summary: They reach Veyra, diminished and half-mortal, guarding the path to the Veilstone. She tests Ada with visions of every life saved and ruined by the covenant's breaking. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: awe curdling into anger at gods who let mortals carry their burdens.

chapters.title: The Keystone's Weight
chapters.summary: Veyra explains the forging: the keystone memory must be willingly surrendered at the Veilstone—every recollection tied to Ada's loved ones, dissolved into the covenant. Kaelen begs her to refuse; they could flee beyond the gods' reach. POV: Kaelen. Emotional beat: desperate love against inevitable duty.

chapters.title: Maren at the Gates
chapters.summary: Maren's army reaches the Veil's approach, intending to destroy the Veilstone and sever the realms forever—an act that would kill every god, including the benign ones sustaining harvests and healing. Ada must ally with the very faith Maren despises. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: conviction beginning to fracture as she sees the human cost.

chapters.title: Battle of the Broken Shrine
chapters.summary: A running battle through the Veil's approaches; smugglers, villagers freed from loops, and remnant faithful defend the mountain while Ada climbs toward the Veilstone. Sorrel's old guild brothers die holding the pass. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: fury and gratitude—her invisible people choosing to be seen.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Veilstone
chapters.summary: At the summit, Ada faces Maren alone among the stones. Instead of fighting, Ada shows her the memories the keystone holds—centuries of covenant kept and betrayed. Maren wavers, then stands aside, undone not by force but witness. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: triumph of empathy over ideology.

chapters.title: The Surrendering
chapters.summary: As the thirteenth turn completes, Ada gives her memories to the Veilstone: her mother's lullabies, Sorrel's lessons, Kaelen's laugh. The covenant reforges; the gods wake whole and bounded by new terms. She descends the mountain knowing something precious is gone but not what. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: devastating serenity—sacrifice complete, self hollowed.

chapters.title: A Stranger's Kindness
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Ada runs her roads again, content but haunted by gaps. A familiar stranger appears at her fire, patient and grieving: Kaelen, fully mortal now, whom she does not remember loving. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: bittersweet hope—love outlasting memory.

chapters.title: What Kaelen Kept
chapters.summary: Kaelen shares the records he made: letters, sketches, songs documenting everything Ada lost. Reading them, she feels echoes without recall. She chooses to keep traveling with this kind stranger rather than send him away. POV: Kaelen. Emotional beat: devotion without expectation, grief without bitterness.

chapters.title: The First New Prayer
chapters.summary: Under the renewed covenant, the old gods answer gently again. At a rebuilt shrine, Ada makes a prayer of her own—not for her memories back, but for the strength to build new ones. The flame answers warmly. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: acceptance and quiet grace.

chapters.title: Noor and the Veil
chapters.summary: Years on, Ada teaches young wardens the hidden roads while Kaelen chronicles the new covenant. One dawn, a scent or song sparks a flicker of true remembering—her mother's voice, one clear note. She smiles, keeps walking, and lets the rest come slowly. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: hard-won peace; memory as a road still being traveled.
